catholic-encyclopedia-1913-john-of-nikiu:
John of Nikiu was an Egyptian chronicler of the late seventh century whose history preserves the Arab conquest of Egypt. Little is known of him beyond Severus of Ashmunein's History of the Patriarchs. He served under three patriarchs, became Bishop of Nikiu in the Delta and general administrator of Egypt's monasteries. He was then deposed by Patriarch Simeon after disciplining a monk so harshly that he died ten days later.

His Chronicle, written before his deposition, runs from Adam to the Arab conquest. Often copying Byzantine chroniclers such as Malalas and John of Antioch, it still preserves Egyptian traditions. It gives details on the fall of Phocas, the accession of Heraclius, seventh-century Egypt, and the Arab conquest itself, told little after the events. Written in Greek with Coptic chapters on Egypt, it survives only in an Ethiopic version made in 1602 from a lost Arabic text.
podcast-dannyjones-QJiYc-6XcIU:
The researcher known as UAP Gerb joins Danny Jones to discuss deep sea alien bases and what he calls the underwater CIA project no one talks about. His case assembles naval reports, sonar lore, and declassified fragments into a claim that the oceans hide both non-human occupants and the American programs watching them.

Jones follows the evidence piece by piece, asking which documents exist and which are rumored. The documented core here is thin and the construction on top of it is Gerb's, preserved as his presentation. The ocean setting does real work in the argument: most of the seafloor is unmapped, so absence of evidence feels weaker there. Listeners fascinated by the underwater turn in UFO culture get one of its main researchers laying out the full claim, in the depths where verification goes to die.
podcast-tuckercarlson-XwBMKwt14IU:
John Kiriakou, a former CIA officer who went to prison for leaking, joins Tucker Carlson for a long interview. The title lists the CIA torture program, MK-Ultra, and the attacks of September 11. It also asks why President Obama sent him to jail.

Kiriakou tells how he helped catch terror suspects, then broke ranks over torture. He explains his leak, his trial, and his time in prison in his own words. Carlson draws out his views on the agency he once served. Listeners get a rare first hand account from a man who paid a high price for speaking out.
